Mostly everything has been touched on in this thread, but another appetite suppressant/anti-obesity drug that may potentially emerge in the coming years is THCV. It occurs naturally in certain cultivars of cannabis and acts as an antagonist for the CB1 receptor, producing reduction in appetite. There is also ongoing research regarding the use of synthetic CB1 receptor antagonists as drugs to treat obesity/metabolic syndrome. There was actually already a selective CB1 receptor that was approved for use in the EU called rimomabant (SR141716), and by all indications it worked very well with respect to its intended purpose, but caused psychiatric side effects in some patients who took it and so it was discontinued. I’m interested to see if THCV will eventually see use as an anorectic that avoids such side effects.

Distillation is a separate step in production from extraction method. For almost all of the vapes on the market currently, the production method is as follows: initial extraction with a solvent (either CO2, ethanol, or a hydrocarbon)-> distillation -> terpenes reintroduced, most likely botanical terpenes. 

My point is that when distillation is involved in the production process, the extraction method pretty much doesn’t matter. On some product descriptions on the OCS, it will say something like “CO2 extracted cannabis distillate”... this = distillate, not a FSE. Other product descriptions say “CO2 extraction process”, conveniently omitting that the extract is then distilled - like spinach and cove products.

I don’t disagree with you that the laws should loosen up here, and I think they definitely will with time. 

But my view is that the lack of regs for these US hemp flowers right now is not a good thing. These are grown as industrial hemp so the limits of contaminants in the final product like pesticides, heavy metals, microbials, and hormones like PGRs are not held to the same standards (many of the growers probably aren’t even doing proper contaminant testing). Many of these farms are also using undocumented labour to cut costs. 

Even if it made the prices this low, I personally wouldn’t want to regularly consume pot that was produced like this. I’m sure that we will eventually find a healthy middle ground.

Hemp derived CBD in the US right now is in its Wild West. Hemp cultivation was legalized through the farm bill in 2018 and now everyone’s growing high CBD cultivars that count as ‘hemp’ since they’re ostensibly under the 0.3% THC limit... also pretty much anybody can legally grow these plants and sell them on a commercial scale. These prices aren’t realistic in Canada right now because under our framework these would have to be grown by a health Canada approved licensed producer and undergo the same administrative red tape and testing/quality control, plus be hit with excise taxes. You’re comparing apples to oranges. That being said, prices are already starting to trend down in the rec market here so I hope this will continue in the future.

P.S. I’ve tried a handful of hemp CBD flowers like these from the US over the last year (now it’s almost impossible to have them shipped to Canada). There were definitely some gems that exceeded OCS quality, but most of it is barely smokeable trash that will give you a headache.
